picks.why: Procházka brings proven elite championship experience and relentless forward pressure.
Procházka generates heavy volume and unpredictable power angles from both stances.
Both men carry finishing power that often leads to an early stoppage.
This matchup is likely to be decided in chaotic kickboxing exchanges on the feet.
Procházka's high-variance style and power favor an outcome well before the final horn.
Hooker holds the height and reach advantages and operates effectively behind straight punches and intercepting knees.
Ortega is extremely durable and rarely gets knocked out cold, making a grueling decision likely.
Both fighters absorb and land high volume across three full rounds.
Hooker possesses solid takedown defense and Ortega does not rely on high-volume wrestling shots.
Both veterans are renowned for their durability and ability to weather heavy damage.

costInfo: Now: free plan, $0. Same-game parlays need player props, which cost 5 credits per game (points, rebounds, assists, threes, 20+ style milestones). The free plan covers props for 2 games a day on average (3 a day for the rest of this month, since credits carried over). Slips are built from the best of those games.
Upgrade option (not done): The Odds API 20K plan, $30 USD a month (about $42 CAD). Gives props for every NBA game every day (about 1,300 credits a month used), so slips can come from any game.

UFC: the feed carries fight winner and, at some books, total rounds. It does NOT carry method of victory, significant strikes or takedowns on any plan, so UFC underdog picks are tracked as straight wins.
Grading costs no odds credits: NBA results and box scores come from ESPN's free public data; UFC results from a sourced Google search.
Credits left are checked before every call; it stops spending 25 credits before the limit and posts fewer prop games instead.
